source.author: lucan
source.text: Quacumque vagatur, Sanguineum veluti quatiens Bellone flagellum, Bistonas aut Mavors agitans, si verbere saevo Palladia stimulet turbatos aegide currus, Nox ingens scelerum, et caedes oriuntur, et instar Immensae vocis gemitus, et pondere lapsi Pectoris arma sonant, confractique ensibus enses.
source.text_original: Quacumque vagatur, / Sanguineum veluti quatiens Bellone flagellum, / Bistonas aut Mavors agitans, si verbere saevo / Palladia stimulet turbatos aegide currus, / Nox ingens scelerum, et caedes oriuntur, et instar / Immensae vocis gemitus, et pondere lapsi / Pectoris arma sonant, confractique ensibus enses.
source.text_english: Wherever she roams, as though brandishing a bloodstained scourge, whether Bellona or Mavors driving on the Bistones, if with savage lash Palladia goads the upset chariots of her aegis, there arise a vast night of crimes and slaughter, and groans like an immense voice, and arms fall with the weight of a shattered breast, and swords are broken by swords.

reuse.text: via facta per undas perque hiemes, Bellona, tibi.
reuse.text_original: via facta per undas / perque hiemes, Bellona, tibi.
reuse.text_english: a road made through the waves and through the winters, O Bellona, for you.
